title: What the JVM is and how it works
answer: The JVM, or Java Virtual Machine, is the runtime that executes Java bytecode. Java source is first compiled into `.class` files containing bytecode. When the application starts, the JVM loads the required classes, verifies bytecode for structural and safety rules, links and initializes classes, and then executes bytecode using interpretation and just-in-time compilation so frequently executed paths can become native machine code. The JVM also provides runtime services such as memory areas, garbage collection, threads, exceptions, security/runtime checks, and interaction with native operating-system resources. The JVM is a specification with platform-specific implementations, which is why the same compatible bytecode can run on different operating systems with an appropriate JVM.
